questions.question: Shareholders and stakeholders differ because:
options: A. Shareholders own shares; stakeholders are everyone affected by the firm
B. The two words mean the same group
C. Stakeholders are only the directors
D. Shareholders never care about profit
questions.explanation: Shareholders are one stakeholder group. Employees, customers, suppliers and the community are stakeholders too, even when they own no shares.

questions.question: A firm advertises a ‘biodegradable’ bag that does not break down as claimed. This is best called:
questions.explanation: Greenwashing is a misleading environmental claim. Diversification is entering a new market. Limited liability is a legal feature of a company, not an advertising practice.

questions.question: Two stakeholder aims clash when a café raises wages and keeps prices unchanged. The clash is:
options: A. Every stakeholder is better off
B. Employees gain while owners may earn less profit
D. The government becomes the owner
questions.explanation: Higher wages without higher prices squeeze profit. That is a stakeholder conflict, not a result that helps every group.
questions.subject: bafs

questions.question: A sole proprietor is personally responsible for the business debts. That liability is:
options: A. Limited to the price of one share
B. Limited to the amount of a bank deposit
D. Shared automatically with every customer
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor and the business are not separate legal persons. Business debts can be claimed from the owner’s personal assets.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A private limited company, compared with a sole proprietor, generally:
options: A. Is a separate legal entity and cannot offer shares to the public
B. Must offer shares to the public
C. Has unlimited liability for every shareholder
D. Cannot have more than one owner
questions.explanation: A private company is a separate legal person. It does not invite the public to subscribe for shares; that public offer is a feature of a listed or public company route.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: In a general partnership, a partner’s liability for the firm’s debts is usually:
options: A. Limited to the capital the partner promised, with no further risk
B. Zero, because only the firm is sued
C. Limited to one month of profit
questions.explanation: General partners can be required to meet business debts beyond what they invested. A limited partner in a limited partnership is a different arrangement and is not the default general partner.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A franchisee typically receives:
options: A. Automatic limited liability, whatever the legal form
B. The right to use a brand and an operating system, in return for fees
D. Exemption from all Hong Kong business law
questions.explanation: The franchise is a right to trade under someone else’s brand and system. It does not by itself change the franchisee’s legal form or cancel local law.

questions.explanation: The workforce is inside the firm, so it is a strength. An opportunity would be something outside, such as a new market.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: The 4Ps are:
options: A. Profit, plan, people and process only
B. Assets, liabilities, capital and drawings
C. Product, price, place and promotion
D. Recruitment, selection, training and appraisal
questions.explanation: The basic marketing mix is product, price, place and promotion. People, process and physical evidence extend it for services. The other lists are accounting or human resources.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Market segmentation means:
options: A. Dividing a market into groups with similar needs
B. Selling one product at one price to everyone with no groups
C. Closing the least profitable shop
questions.explanation: Segmentation groups buyers so the firm can design a clearer offer. It is not a ratio and it is not the same as exiting a location.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A skimming price is:
options: A. A permanently low price to gain the whole market
B. A price equal to variable cost
C. A discount that is illegal
D. A high opening price aimed at buyers who will pay more at launch
questions.explanation: Skimming takes a high price while some buyers are keen, then often lowers it later. A low entry price to gain share is penetration.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Place in the marketing mix is about:
options: A. Only the city where the head office is registered
B. How the product reaches the customer
C. The font on the poster
questions.explanation: Place is distribution: channels, coverage and logistics. The poster’s design is promotion. The registered city is not the whole of place.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: MPF in Hong Kong is:
options: A. A voluntary tip paid only in December
B. A type of share capital
C. A mandatory retirement-savings scheme with contributions from employer and employee
questions.explanation: The Mandatory Provident Fund requires regular contributions so employees accumulate retirement savings. It is not share capital and not a discount.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: On-the-job training happens:
options: A. At the workplace, while doing the work
B. Only in a classroom away from the firm
C. Only before a person is hired
questions.explanation: On-the-job training uses the real workplace. Off-the-job training is the classroom or outside course. Induction can include both, but the phrase itself means at work.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A job description mainly sets out:
options: B. Only the preferred age of the candidate
D. Duties and responsibilities of the post
questions.explanation: The description is about the job. A person specification is about the candidate. Age limits can raise discrimination issues and are not the definition of the description.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: High staff turnover often signals:
options: A. That training is no longer needed
B. Costs of repeated recruitment and a possible problem with conditions or morale
C. Higher gross profit by definition
D. That MPF can be cancelled
questions.explanation: Replacing people costs money and can mean the job or the management is unsatisfactory. It does not automatically raise gross profit, and it does not remove MPF duties.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: The accounting equation is:
questions.explanation: What the firm owns equals what it owes outsiders plus the owner’s residual interest. Income and expenses affect profit, which then changes capital. The current ratio is a different statement.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: The owner takes goods for personal use. The double entry is:
options: A. Debit drawings, credit purchases or inventory
D. No entry, because the owner owns the firm
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce capital. If inventory is taken, inventory (or purchases) is credited. It is not a sale to a customer, and it still needs an entry.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A credit purchase of inventory:
options: A. Increases cash and increases capital
C. Is recorded only when the supplier is paid
D. Increases inventory and increases trade payables
questions.explanation: On credit, the firm receives inventory and owes the supplier. Cash does not move until payment. Accrual records the purchase when it happens, not only when cash is paid.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Revenue is recognised when:
options: B. It is earned, not necessarily when cash arrives
C. A non-current asset is bought
questions.explanation: Accrual accounting records revenue when the goods or services are delivered. Cash may arrive earlier or later. Drawings and asset purchases are not revenue.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Gross profit equals:
options: A. Sales minus every expense including rent
C. Sales minus cost of goods sold
D. Cash inflows minus cash outflows
questions.explanation: Gross profit stops at the trading items: net sales less the cost of the goods sold. Rent and other operating expenses come after that, in the move toward net profit. The statement of financial position is not a profit figure.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: An income statement covers:
options: B. One moment only, with no period
questions.explanation: Profit is earned over a period, so the heading carries ‘for the year ended’. A statement of financial position is at a date.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A statement of financial position shows:
options: A. Only sales and cost of goods sold
D. Assets, liabilities and capital at a date
questions.explanation: It is the position on one date: what is owned, what is owed, and the owner’s capital. Sales belong in the income statement.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Closing inventory appears in the financial statements as:
options: A. An expense in full, with nothing left on the statement of financial position
B. A deduction in cost of goods sold and a current asset
questions.explanation: Unsold goods are not a cost of this period’s sales. They reduce cost of goods sold and remain a current asset. They are not a liability and not drawings.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Current ratio equals:
questions.explanation: The current ratio compares short-term resources with short-term obligations. Inverting it is not the ratio. Gross profit over sales is a margin.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: The quick (acid-test) ratio typically removes:
options: C. Trade payables from current liabilities
questions.explanation: Inventory may not turn into cash quickly. The acid test uses current assets minus inventory, over current liabilities. Removing cash would hide the most liquid asset.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Gross profit margin equals:
options: C. Cost of goods sold ÷ inventory
questions.explanation: The margin shows how much of each sales dollar remains after the cost of goods. Inventory turnover uses cost of goods sold and inventory. Current ratio is liquidity, not a margin.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A higher gearing ratio means:
options: A. More cash in the current account
B. More long-term debt relative to capital employed
C. A higher gross profit margin by definition
D. That the firm has no interest to pay
questions.explanation: Gearing measures how far long-term finance comes from debt. Higher gearing means more fixed interest and more financial risk. It is not a profit margin and it does not mean interest has disappeared.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A personal budget is useful because it:
options: A. Replaces the need for any saving
B. Is the same document as a company’s statement of financial position
C. Compares expected income and spending before the money is gone
questions.explanation: A budget shows whether planned spending fits planned income. It does not promise investment returns, and it is not a company’s balance sheet.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: An ethical decision can be legal and still be:
options: A. Open to criticism if it harms stakeholders the law does not fully protect
B. Impossible, because law and ethics are identical
questions.explanation: Law is a minimum. A harsh contract or a misleading claim can be legal in a narrow sense and still fail an ethics test. Ethics does not guarantee higher profit.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: Diversifying personal savings means:
options: A. Borrowing the maximum the bank will lend
B. Keeping every dollar in one stock
D. Not putting all the money into one asset
questions.explanation: Spreading money across assets reduces the damage if one of them falls. One stock is the opposite. Borrowing the maximum raises risk rather than spreading it.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper

questions.question: A conflict of interest for an employee arises when:
options: A. The employee follows the staff code
B. A private interest could bias a decision the employee makes for the employer
C. The firm publishes its prices
D. The current ratio is above 1
questions.explanation: The problem is a personal benefit that may pull the decision away from the employer’s interest. Following a code is the control, not the conflict.
questions.subject: bafs
questions.syllabus_ref: HKDSE BAFS — original drill, not an HKEAA paper
